question: A 42-year-old man is brought to the emergency department by the police after he was involved in a physical altercation at a friend’s home. Upon physical examination, the patient is disheveled. He is very agitated and actively strikes out at nurses and other hospital staff. A decision is made to place him in restraints. Head, eyes, ears, nose, and throat exam reveals temporal wasting, marked tooth decay, and healing and new ulcers in his mouth and on his lips. His pupils are dilated and minimally reactive to light. His skin shows dramatic diaphoresis as well as excoriations over his arms. Vital signs show pulse of 120/min, respirations of 12/min, temperature of 39.0°C (102.2°F), and blood pressure of 150/100 mm Hg. Urine drug screen is positive for an amphetamine. Which of the following is a life-threatening complication of the toxicity seen in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Amphetamine toxicity" -> "increased sympathetic activity" -> "elevated heart rate" -> "increased body temperature" -> "hyperthermia" -> "heat stroke" -> 80% CHAIN: "Amphetamine toxicity" -> "increased sympathetic activity" -> "dilated pupils" -> "minimally reactive to light" -> "autonomic dysfunction" -> "malignant hyperthermia" -> 75% CHAIN: "Amphetamine toxicity" -> "increased sympathetic activity" -> "respiratory stimulation" -> "tachypnea" -> "respiratory alkalosis" -> "respiratory depression" -> 70% CHAIN: "Amphetamine toxicity" -> "increased sympathetic activity" -> "seizure threshold lowering" -> "seizure" -> 60% CHAIN: "Amphetamine toxicity" -> "increased sympathetic activity" -> "cardiac stimulation" -> "tachycardia" -> "arrhythmia" -> "sudden cardiac arrest" -> 80%
enhanced_information: In a patient with amphetamine toxicity, life-threatening complications can include heat stroke due to increased body temperature, malignant hyperthermia from autonomic dysfunction, respiratory depression from respiratory alkalosis, seizure from lowered seizure threshold, and sudden cardiac arrest from arrhythmias caused by cardiac stimulation.
analysis: In a patient with amphetamine toxicity, the most likely life-threatening complication is sudden cardiac arrest due to arrhythmias caused by cardiac stimulation. While heat stroke and malignant hyperthermia can also be serious, sudden cardiac arrest is a more immediate and direct consequence of amphetamine toxicity.
